$ healthcli 
healthcli imports your Apple Health export into a local SQLite database
and lets you log, review and query your data. Nothing leaves your machine.

Exit codes:
  0  ok
  1  runtime error
  2  usage error (bad arguments, bad flags, unknown command)
  3  database not found

With --json an error is printed on stdout as
{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}} and nothing else.

Usage:
  healthcli [command]

Examples:
  healthcli import apple export.zip
  healthcli log weight 72.5
  healthcli today
  healthcli overview
  healthcli trend steps --days 30
  healthcli query "SELECT * FROM samples LIMIT 5" --json

Available Commands:
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  heatmap     Calendar heatmap of one metric, one cell per day
  help        Help about any command
  import      Import data from another source
  log         Record a manual measurement
  overview    One-screen summary of every metric, sleep, workouts and data health
  query       Run a read-only SQL query
  sleep       Last night's sleep: hypnogram, stats against your usual, calendar
  today       Show a day's summary compared with your baseline
  trend       Show how a metric changes over the last days
  version     Print the healthcli version
  workouts    Workouts: type table, weekly volume, bests, recent sessions and a calendar

Flags:
      --db string   SQLite database path (default: per-user data dir)
  -h, --help        help for healthcli
      --json        output JSON instead of human-readable text

Use "healthcli [command] --help" for more information about a command.

$ healthcli help trend
Show one metric over the last N days as a sparkline (a dot marks a day without
data), with min, max and mean, the last 7 days against the 7 before, and the
baseline (the 28 days before the last day, as in overview and today). On a
pipe, or with --ascii, the sparkline uses plain ASCII characters instead of
block bars (_ marks a day without data). With colour on, the bars use the same
palette as the heatmaps: the hue of the metric (heart red, respiratory cyan,
sleep blue, body purple and violet, orange for activity), dim for low days and
bright for high ones.

Metrics: heart_rate, resting_heart_rate, step_count, hrv_sdnn, body_mass, active_energy, respiratory_rate, apple_sleeping_wrist_temperature, oxygen_saturation, vo2_max, walking_heart_rate_average, heart_rate_recovery_one_minute, blood_pressure_systolic, blood_pressure_diastolic, blood_glucose, basal_energy, apple_exercise_time, apple_stand_time, flights_climbed, distance_walking_running, time_in_daylight, body_fat_percentage, body_mass_index, lean_body_mass, height, walking_speed, walking_step_length, walking_asymmetry, walking_double_support, apple_walking_steadiness, sleep (hours asleep per night).
Aliases: hr, hrv, rhr, rr, spo2, steps, temp, vo2, weight, bmi.

Pages fit 50 to 100 columns ($COLUMNS or the terminal width); a narrower
terminal is treated as 50, so lines may wrap there.

The window ends today unless --date says otherwise. With --verbose, a table
lists every day with its value and source.

JSON output (--json) has these fields:
  status      "ok", or "no_data" if the window is empty (then latest_day says where data is)
  metric, unit, from, to, days
  daily[]     day, value (null on a gap), source        one entry per day
  summary     days_with_data, min, min_day, max, max_day, mean   (null if no data)
  change_7d   available, last7_mean, last7_days_with_data, previous7_mean,
              previous7_days_with_data, delta, delta_pct
  baseline    available, days_with_data, days_needed, mean   (the 28 days before "to")
Sleep values are hours asleep.

Usage:
  healthcli trend <metric> [flags]

Examples:
  healthcli trend steps
  healthcli trend weight --days 90
  healthcli trend sleep --verbose
  healthcli trend hr --days 14 --json

Flags:
      --ascii         use plain ASCII characters only
      --date string   last day of the window, YYYY-MM-DD (default: today)
      --days int      number of days to show (default 30)
  -h, --help          help for trend
      --no-color      never use colours
  -v, --verbose       also print a per-day table

Global Flags:
      --db string   SQLite database path (default: per-user data dir)
      --json        output JSON instead of human-readable text
$ healthcli help import apple
Import an Apple Health export file. In the Health app on your iPhone choose
your profile picture, then "Export All Health Data", and pass the resulting file here.

The file is streamed, so even multi-gigabyte exports use little memory.
Importing the same file again adds nothing new. A record whose key (type,
times, source) is already stored is not imported again; if its value differs
from the stored one it is counted as a conflict, and the stored value stays.

Before the first write into a database that already holds data, a safety copy
is made next to it (<database>.bak, readable only by you, replaced on every
import). Use --no-backup to skip it, for example when the database is huge
and you have your own backups.

--dry-run reads the whole file and prints the counts a real import would give,
but writes nothing (and makes no backup).

Press Ctrl-C to stop an import: the rows read so far stay saved, and running
the same import again finishes it. A byte that is not valid UTF-8 is replaced
with U+FFFD and counted instead of stopping the import.

Usage:
  healthcli import apple <export.zip|export.xml> [flags]

Examples:
  healthcli import apple export.zip
  healthcli import apple export.zip --dry-run
  healthcli import apple export.xml --json

Flags:
      --dry-run     read and count everything, write nothing
  -h, --help        help for apple
      --no-backup   do not copy the database to <database>.bak before importing

Global Flags:
      --db string   SQLite database path (default: per-user data dir)
      --json        output JSON instead of human-readable text

$ healthcli completion
Generate the autocompletion script for healthcli for the specified shell.
See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.

Usage:
  healthcli completion [command]

Available Commands:
  bash        Generate the autocompletion script for bash
  fish        Generate the autocompletion script for fish
  powershell  Generate the autocompletion script for powershell
  zsh         Generate the autocompletion script for zsh

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for completion

Global Flags:
      --db string   SQLite database path (default: per-user data dir)
      --json        output JSON instead of human-readable text
